scope: Frozen offline wrapper and its two test files only; accepted core interfaces inspected only to reproduce wrapper integration defects

findings.title: A first cancellation can bypass wrapper recovery after successful cutover effects
findings.detail: When provisional publication fails after Installer.run succeeds, runner.recovering remains false until the wrapper's exception suite sets it. A first SIGINT/SIGTERM delivered on entry to that suite invokes cancel(), which raises Refused out of the already-active except handler. No outer handler runs rollback or emits the sanitized summary. The finally block closes the runtime but does not restore the original services.
findings.reproduction: Use the real wrapper and real Installer.run over the existing synthetic entrypoint fixture. Force _publish to raise, then inject the installed cancellation callback at the first exception-suite line before recovering is set. Observed Refused escape, zero rollback calls, zero original apps running/four originals exited, four prepared apps still running, and no JSON summary.
findings.shortest_correction: Make the exception-to-recovery handoff itself cancellation-safe: latch/defer cancellation during failure handling, not only once runner.recovering is true. Ensure an initial signal at this handoff cannot escape owned recovery. Add a deterministic regression at this exact boundary without changing accepted core or resetting deadlines.

findings.title: Cancellation and failure cleanup assume an already initialized runner
findings.detail: Installer.__init__ creates used=False but no recovering or ownership sets. Installer._initialize sets used=True before recovering and other fields. Cancellation after used=True but before recovering exists raises AttributeError in cancel(); the wrapper's cleanup condition then accesses the same missing attribute and raises again. Similar guard assumptions exist for quiesced/quiesce_pending during partial initialization.
findings.reproduction: Inject the installed SIGINT callback in _initialize immediately after used=True and before plan/images assignment. Observed uncaught AttributeError, no JSON summary and no rollback. All four originals remain running and no replacements have started, so this case is before effects.
findings.shortest_correction: Make cancellation and outer failure handling tolerate partial initialization; used alone is not proof that recovery/ownership fields exist. Keep this early failure sanitized and avoid invoking rollback before effects. Add an initialization-boundary regression.

verification.synthetic_repro_command:
env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 ./.venv/bin/python -B - <<'PY'
import contextlib, inspect, io, json, os, signal, sys, tempfile
from pathlib import Path
import pytest
from tests.test_companion_cutover_entrypoint import setup, entry, install
results=[]
for scenario in ("signal_during_initialize", "signal_entering_publication_failure_recovery"):
 with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="cutover-review-repro-") as tmp, pytest.MonkeyPatch.context() as mp:
  s=setup.__wrapped__(Path(tmp),mp)
  fired=[]
  if scenario=="signal_entering_publication_failure_recovery":
   def publication_failure(*args): raise OSError("SYNTHETIC_PUBLICATION_FAILURE")
   mp.setattr(entry,"_publish",publication_failure)
  filename=str(Path(entry.__file__).resolve())
  initcode=install.Installer._initialize.__code__
  lines,start=inspect.getsourcelines(install.Installer._initialize)
  initline=start+next(i for i,line in enumerate(lines) if "self.plan, self.images =" in line)
  source=Path(filename).read_text().splitlines()
  exceptline=next(i for i,line in enumerate(source,1) if "if runner is not None and runner.used" in line)
  def trace(frame,event,arg):
   hit=(scenario=="signal_during_initialize" and frame.f_code is initcode and frame.f_lineno==initline
        or scenario=="signal_entering_publication_failure_recovery" and frame.f_code.co_filename==filename and frame.f_lineno==exceptline)
   if event=="line" and hit and not fired:
    fired.append(True);sys.settrace(None)
    s.handlers[signal.SIGINT](signal.SIGINT,None)
   return trace
  fd,writer=os.pipe();os.close(writer)
  output=io.StringIO();escaped=None;exitcode=None
  try:
   with contextlib.redirect_stdout(output):
    sys.settrace(trace)
    exitcode=entry.main([*s.args,"--execute-cutover","--token-fd",str(fd)])
  except BaseException as e:
   escaped=type(e).__name__
  finally:
   sys.settrace(None)
   try:os.close(fd)
   except OSError:pass
  originals={r.id for r in s.plan.baseline[3:]}
  replacements={r.id for r in s.prepared.replacements}
  result={"scenario":scenario,"injection_fired":bool(fired),"escaped_exception":escaped,"exit_code":exitcode,
   "stdout_summary_present":bool(output.getvalue()),"rollback_calls":len(s.rollbacks),
   "original_apps_running":sum(r.id in originals and r.state=="running" for r in s.backend.rows.values()),
   "prepared_apps_running":sum(r.id in replacements and r.state=="running" for r in s.backend.rows.values()),
   "original_apps_exited":sum(r.id in originals and r.state=="exited" for r in s.backend.rows.values()),
   "runtime_closed":s.closed==[True],"native_operations":False}
  assert result["injection_fired"] and not result["stdout_summary_present"] and result["rollback_calls"]==0
  if scenario=="signal_entering_publication_failure_recovery":
   assert result["original_apps_exited"]==4 and result["prepared_apps_running"]==4
  results.append(result)
print(json.dumps({"synthetic_only":True,"results":results},indent=2))
PY

shown_non_blocking_checks: Default input validation is separate from token/lock/reservation/native construction, and uses existing Plan, ReviewedPreparation and runtime-policy schemas.
Saved metadata must reproduce the reviewed stopped Snapshots; only logical aliases are modeled and both the raw pre-start runtime pin and configured manifest fingerprint are cross-bound.

The focused tests cover synthetic real-controller success/recovery, token-reader stubbing, lock/marker durability and replay refusal, sanitation, ordinary publication/commit failures and signals delivered after recovery is already active.
limits: Passing focused tests do not cover the two demonstrated asynchronous handoff boundaries and are not acceptance.

Reproductions use disposable temporary files, synthetic token reader/policy inputs, fake native/runtime state and installed callback injection; no OS signals were sent to native services and no real lifecycle or credential call occurred.
No real runtime policy/dependency/topical packet is approved or manufactured. Native SDK, alias, endpoint and full execution feasibility remain UNVERIFIED.
No accepted core source, reviewed wrapper/tests or previous evidence was edited. Review receipt and visible work log are the only reviewer edits.
